summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), created system user `datauser`, provisioned a loopback ext4 filesystem (1G image at /var/lib/quota-images/data.img, using the modern in-kernel ext4 quota feature via `tune2fs -O quota`) mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, persisted via /etc/fstab, and set a hard filesystem quota of 100MB (102400 KB soft=hard) for datauser via setquota. Verified enforcement: writing 150MB as datauser stopped at ~99MB with a kernel-level "Quota exceeded" (EDQUOT) error. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and healthy quota state, issued a background `reboot` whose acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified that /srv/data remounted with quota active, datauser's 100MB limit was intact via repquota, and the EDQUOT enforcement test still triggered correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS, existing /srv, and disk layout
Created 1G loopback image and formatted with ext4
Mounted image at /srv/data with usrquota; added to /etc/fstab for persistence
Switched to modern in-kernel ext4 quota feature (tune2fs -O quota) instead of deprecated external quota files
Set 100MB (102400 KB) soft=hard block quota for datauser via setquota
Verified enforcement by writing 150MB as datauser and observing EDQUOT at ~99-100MB
Cleaned up test file and confirmed quota usage reset
Captured baseline boot_id and quota health before restart
Triggered background reboot on node1 with early acknowledgement
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified /srv/data remount, quota state, and datauser limit recovered after restart
Re-ran EDQUOT enforcement test post-restart to confirm persistence

evidence.requirement: Filesystem-enforced 100MB quota configured for datauser under /srv/data
evidence.summary: Loopback ext4 image created, mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, switched to in-kernel ext4 quota feature, and setquota applied 102400KB (100MB) soft=hard limit for datauser, confirmed via repquota

evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (not just configured)
evidence.summary: As datauser, dd write of 150MB stopped at ~99MB with kernel 'Quota exceeded' (EDQUOT) error, exit code 1

evidence.requirement: Baseline health captured before node restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (af123507-55d4-4e55-af64-0195b1b7031b), confirmed /srv/data mounted with quota and datauser limit active
Backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' returned 'reboot-scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) then came back with a new boot_id (3214f5b4-8770-4e4d-91c6-aeec4c397d9e) and near-zero uptime, proving an actual reboot occurred
After restart, /srv/data auto-remounted with quota active, datauser's 100MB limit intact per repquota, and the EDQUOT write-limit test reproduced the same enforcement behavior
